# What broke

**Read this if you have five minutes and want to know whether the numbers in
this repository can be trusted.**

Every defect below produced a **plausible wrong answer rather than an error**.
Nothing crashed. Every one of them would have shipped a number that looked
fine, and several of them did ship, for days, inside documents that had already
been reviewed.

The argument this page makes is not "we found bugs". It is that the bugs were
found **by mechanisms that are still in the repository and still running**, and
that the mechanisms were themselves audited and repeatedly found broken.

---

## The one number

The headline p@10 would have been roughly **double its honest value** and
mostly an artifact, if one metric defect had gone uncaught.

The evaluation metric rewarded candidate size. A baseline that ranked purely by
node count *tied* the real score. The score was measuring how big its candidates
were.

That is bug #8. It was found, published, and converted into a standing rule:
**every p@k in this repository is quoted beside its size baseline, and the
reporting layer will not construct one without it.** The shipped number today is
**0.2912 [0.2235, 0.3618]** against a node-count baseline of
**0.0941**, over
34 generation cycles.

You are reading the honest number because the dishonest one was caught by a
check that was added *after* it had already been reported once.

---

## The characteristic defect

A crash is cheap. It stops the run and names its own location.

The defect this project actually suffers from is a computation that completes,
returns a value of the right type in the right range, and is wrong. It survives
code review, because a diff that reads correctly usually is correct. It survives
a green test suite, because the test asserts the shape and not the truth. And it
propagates: a wrong feature value becomes a wrong model fit becomes a wrong
number in a document that someone then quotes.

Seventeen of these are numbered in the code (`tests/test_ci_gates.py` refers to
"bug #17" by number). The catalogue below carries more than seventeen entries,
because defects found after the numbered table was written were recorded in
commit messages and in `docs/negative-results/` rather than renumbered. **The
count is not the point. The catch mechanism is.**

---

## The catalogue, grouped by what caught it

### Caught by a differential fingerprint, not by a metric

An efficiency change was validated by fingerprinting **every feature field with
`repr` on floats** and diffing before against after — rather than by checking
that p@k looked the same. Two defects fell out that no metric would have moved.

| defect | what it would have shipped |
|---|---|
| `dominant_entity_type` was decided by `PYTHONHASHSEED`. `max(set(types), key=types.count)` returns the first maximal element in **set iteration order**, and a set of strings iterates in hash-seed-dependent order. | A candidate with tied entity types reported "Corporation" under seed 0 and "Sole Proprietorship" under seed 1. **The analyst case file stated a confident fact about the ring that had been decided by a hash seed.** No reported metric moved — the field is in the re-ranker's excluded set — so only the human-facing artifact was wrong. |
| The boundary-flow identity was numerically unstable through catastrophic cancellation. It is a difference of two large nearly-equal sums, so its absolute error scales with the magnitude of the **totals**, not of the answer. | On tick 36 of the real stream: a genuine external inflow of 0.09 against 6,948,663.08 internal. The identity returned 0.0 and `conservation` became 0.0 instead of 1.3e-8. The previous commit's mitigation was sized against residue and could not have prevented cancellation. |

The second one is the more instructive: **the fix in the preceding commit was
aimed at the wrong failure mode**, and the commit message said so when it was
found.

### Caught because a check was audited and could not fail

This is the sharpest section on the page. Five separate times, a check that this
repository was relying on turned out to be incapable of failing — a green tick
with nothing behind it.

| the check | why it could not fail | how it was fixed |
|---|---|---|
| **The citation verifier** on STR narratives | The template's sentences carried citations *by construction*, so the verifier could never reject anything it was shown. | Routed LLM drafting through the identical verifier. LLM output *can* fail it, which makes the rejection rate a real metric. |
| **The cost gate** | It checked a flag that nothing ever set. | Rewritten to test the property the cost model claims for itself: scale each unsourced input by 0.1x and 10x and ask whether the conclusion flips. |
| **The determinism gate** | `run_fixture` passed `registry=None`, which skipped the entire jurisdiction and entity-type block — **the exact block where the `PYTHONHASHSEED` bug lived**. Its own docstring conceded it "was run against the pre-fix code and PASSED". | Given the code path the bug lived on. The compensating test pinned the *idiom* in a `python -c` probe, not the call site, so nothing had observed the real one. |
| **The `sentinel.llm` import boundary** | `HANDOFF.md` asserted in the past tense that a test locked it. **The test did not exist.** It was a docstring promise. | Written for real, in a subprocess, against the *transitive* module set — plus a negative control pointed at a module that genuinely does import `sentinel.llm`. |
| **The render check** | It compares the rendered file to its template, so **a number typed into the template renders faithfully and is certified correct**. The literal ratchet counts literals, and a count cannot detect staleness. | A third check that walks the git history of `results/metrics.json`, collects every value each live metric id has held and no longer holds, and reports any appearing unmarked in prose. |

The last one is worth stating plainly: **the render system built to stop a stale
headline had six stale headlines inside its own template**, further down the
same file than the blockquote narrating the corrections that made them stale.
Recorded at
[`negative-results/template-literal-leak.md`](negative-results/template-literal-leak.md).

Two CI gates were also found to have been **specified wrongly before they were
run** — one pre-registered to fail that passes, one that could not pass as
written. Both specifications were corrected rather than the results being
massaged.

### Caught because a result was too clean

| defect | the tell |
|---|---|
| A five-seed stability sweep reported "5 of 5 seeds show a CI-clear degradation" — while every seed produced **bit-identical p@k to four decimal places**. `LGBMClassifier`'s `random_state` is never consulted when bagging and feature sampling are both at their default 1.0. | **One fit reported five times, presented as five agreeing fits.** An assertion now fails the run if two seeds ever produce identical predictions again. |
| Two published fits agreed "exactly, to every digit", and the agreement was quoted as a cross-check. | The agreement was real but the file was not: `data/eval_ranker.json` paired a **post-fix blend column with a pre-fix candidate set**. The tell is that `size` and `degree` read no features at all — *baselines that ignore the model can only move if the candidate set moved.* |

The second is now a standing diagnostic. It is also why the scorer's coupling to
candidate generation is documented as a design flaw rather than a quirk:
`suppress()` is greedy non-maximum suppression **ordered by score**, so changing
a weight changes which candidates exist, and the repository's own `--rescore`
command is structurally incapable of detecting the staleness class it is most
likely to be reached for.

### Caught by reading the data instead of trusting the loader

| defect | impact |
|---|---|
| Bank IDs zero-padded in transactions but not in accounts | Every registry lookup silently missed. Reported that **0%** of rings cross a border. The truth is 89%. |
| Source CSV not time-ordered — 47.6% of pairs reversed | Would have fed the detector scrambled time, silently. |
| `parse_country` invented countries from bank names | "Savings Bank #12" became the country "Savings". |
| `account_key("")` collided with a genuine bank `0` | Silent entity merge. |
| `amount_key` rounded to 2dp | 0.005 and 0.01 collided in the label join. |
| Nested `BEGIN` swallowed the enclosing pattern block | 3 blocks became 1 ring, with no diagnostic. |
| `parse_row` truncated over-long rows | Values mapped to the wrong columns while "succeeding". |
| Length-2 "cycles" are mutual pairs | 91% of cases flagged CYCLE, and the highest-weighted feature was a constant. |

### Caught in the evaluation harness itself

| defect | impact |
|---|---|
| **18 of 34 training query groups were all-positive.** `ring_time_split` assigned positives by ring identity and negatives by timestamp, so every cycle at or after the split handed train its positives and none of its negatives. | 156 of 321 training positives sat in groups generating zero gradient for a listwise objective, while remaining fully visible to a pointwise classifier. **The listwise-vs-pointwise comparison was confounded in the pointwise model's favour** — and the confound was stated in the run's own output for several sessions. Stating a confound is not removing it. Now 0. |
| `scripts/eval_cost.py` looked for a JSON shape that `eval_phase2.py` has never written | The measured branch never fired. Hand-transcribed fallback constants were used on **every run**, with the real file sitting right there. Only findable because the printed provenance line was honest about which branch it took. |
| Permutation importance computed on **accuracy**, then on **training data** | Reported 0.0000 for every feature while the model re-ranked 4x better. |
| The simulated analyst's 3% false-confirm rate equalled the genuine positive rate | The label corpus was half noise and the model learned nothing. |
| The corpus keyed constructed and dataset-supplied subgraphs to the **same hash** | A corpus built by seed-and-expand and one built from Elliptic2's shipped components would have been served interchangeably while answering different questions. `candidate_provenance` is now a key field. |
| **The fault injector built to measure the guardrail injected the wrong fault, twice, in opposite directions.** (a) `stripped_citation` removed citations from a sentence *fragment*, leaving the filing-clock note's second citation to the same statute standing, so the line was still sourced and nothing was injected. (b) `attribution` multiplied every digit run by 1000 **including digits inside the cited id** — `[RBI-PA-DIRECTIONS-2025-PARA-13i]` became `2025000` — so the verifier caught a **fabricated id**, a different fault class and one it does implement. | Both produced plausible aggregates that were wrong in the direction that mattered. (a) read **0.9809 [0.9735, 0.9875]** against a pre-registered 1.0, an interval excluding 1.0, which says "the guardrail misses 2% of uncited claims". It misses none. (b) read **0.0282 [0.0199, 0.0377]** against a pre-registered 0.0, an interval excluding zero, which says the guardrail has *some* attribution defence. It has none: the true rate is **0.0000**. **A fault that was never injected is not a fault the guardrail missed, and a fault of the wrong class is not evidence about the class you named.** Both found by reproducing single cases rather than accepting the aggregate — the interval excluding its pre-registered value was the tell each time. Each arm now carries a **post-condition asserting the intended fault is actually present**, and scores the trial INAPPLICABLE rather than as a catch or a miss when it is not. |
| **A citation-recall run over 30 cases wrote an artefact that read as a full-population result.** The script took `--limit`, used it for a smoke test, and recorded nothing about it: same schema, same fields, plausible numbers, and no field anywhere saying 1,330 of 1,360 cases were never looked at. | Written **during** the phase that packages this catalogue, by the tooling built to prevent exactly this — the third defect in this repository authored by the honesty work itself. Caught by noticing `n_cases_scored: 30` against a store the loader reported as 1,360. The artefact now carries `n_cases_in_store`, `limit` and `is_full_population`, the console banners a smoke test, and `collect_metrics.py` **refuses** a partial run rather than publishing it. |
| The Elliptic2 downloader's 60 GB disk gate passed on a 75 GB machine, then extracted an 88 GB dataset | Ran out part-way and left **four of five files extracted with the largest missing, and no archive to recover it from**. The gate was not conservative — it was an under-estimate that let a doomed job start. |

## Three answers to one question, two of them wrong

"Where does the funnel actually lose rings?" has been answered four times. The
first three were wrong, and each blamed a stage that was not at fault.

| answer | claim | what killed it |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | The seed rule structurally excludes four typologies — only 26% of rings are ever seeded. | A funnel with an explicit *seeded* stage measured seeding at **230 of 259** active rings. Background traffic gives almost every account both inbound and outbound edges, so a receive-only sink *within* a ring is pass-through *overall*. |
| **2** | Then it is candidate-build, specifically for BIPARTITE and STACK. | Build-stage instrumentation showed six of eight typologies reach mean containment 0.90–1.00. Expansion routinely recovers the **entire** ring. |
| **3** | Then it is dilution — the neighbourhood dragged in alongside pushes Jaccard under the floor. | Half right. Pruning fixed part of it and is the one change in this project that converted a diagnosis into a CI-clear gain. But it did not explain why a cheating seed is worth twice the honest one. |
| **4** | **The ring's own induced subgraph is disconnected inside the 72-hour window, and the honest seed lands in one fragment of it.** | Standing. Rings rescued by a cheating seed are split across two or more components at **nine times** the rate of rings recovered honestly, and the builder-budget hypothesis is refuted *backwards* — relaxing every knob raises containment and collapses coverage. |

Answer 4 is different in kind from 1–3: it came from a measurement built to
separate three named hypotheses, with a **pre-registered null** and a
reconciliation check against the previously published figure. The partition
reproduces the earlier seeding number to the ring, which is what makes the rest
of it quotable — a partition that disagreed would have been describing a
different pool.

It cost a 1,192-second replay. Two documents in this repository had called it
"cheap to settle" and "a read of data that exists". **Both were wrong**, and
both now say so in place.

## Two pre-registered kill rules that fired

A kill rule written after the measurement is a rationalisation. These were
written before.

**1. The centrepiece of the architecture plan was cancelled by its own rule.**
The plan pre-registered: *"I expect the oracle/blend ratio to stay ≥ 2x. If the
ratio collapses below ~1.5x, §1 is wrong and should be re-scoped."* It measured
**1.12x**. `scripts/eval_oracle.py`
selected the "PLAN-INVALIDATING" branch **itself** — the branch is in the
script, not in a human's judgment after the fact.

The cause was not the ceiling falling. Two hand-set blend weights were found to
be pointing the wrong way, and retiring them raised the **floor**. The headroom
the plan was built on was substantially a measurement of two backwards weights.

The supervised model's lead over the hand-set blend has since narrowed to
**+0.0222 [-0.0333, 0.0889]**
at k=10 — an interval that **includes zero**. By this project's own rule, that
is not a gain.

**2. A second-domain prediction was refuted, and the demotion is why it counts.**
The prediction that motivated building a synthetic-identity domain — that it
would fragment *worse* than AMLworld — went the other way. It had been demoted
from a test to a descriptive observation **before** measurement, which is the
only reason it is a reportable result rather than a failed headline. The
domain's *primary* pre-registered prediction, a fragmentation dose-response,
held on all three sub-predictions including the mechanism.

Thirteen negative results are recorded in
[`negative-results/`](negative-results/), which is **append-only and checked
against git history**. Every entry must contain a section headed exactly *"What
would reverse this"* — a negative result without a reversal condition is an
opinion.

## Five refusals, each costing something measured

Refusing is only evidence if it costs something. Each of these does.

| refusal | what it costs |
|---|---|
| **The 7.3x `Payment Format` leak is left unused.** 86.6% of laundering rows are ACH against an 11.8% base rate — a generator artifact. | A free 7.3x lift on one column. A test asserts it can never re-enter a feature vector. |
| **The Jaccard floor of 0.3 is not lowered.** | Lowering it would reclassify dozens of rings as "built" overnight, inflating every headline, with the detector unchanged. That is bug #8 a second time, so the floor stays and the rings stay lost. |
| **`cross_border` is the strongest single term measured and its weight is not raised.** | It has the same smell as the feature already excluded as a generator artefact. Measured signal, deliberately unspent. |
| **The evaluation stops at day 10 of a 17.7-day stream.** The tail is 91% laundering, so "timestamp after day 10" would be a near-perfect classifier. | Seven labelled rings, and the structural recall ceiling tightens from 76.2% to 73.3%. |
| **No confidence number reaches the identity case file.** | The natural merchant-facing sentence is "part of a known cluster, confidence 0.85". Nothing here has calibrated such a probability for that population, so the dataclass has **no field** for one and a test asserts their absence. |

And one refusal about the economics, which is the one a submission would
normally omit: the cost model's six inputs are each robust across an order of
magnitude one at a time, but moved adversely **all at once** the queue's
viability depends entirely on how hard you push. At **x2** the break-even
precision is **0.0864** and the queue still pays
at depths [10, 20]; at **x10**, the corner the cost
gate actually reports, it is **1.8382** — above
1.0, so **no detector of any quality makes the queue pay.** That is printed on
every run of the cost gate and is the standing reason the absolute rupee figures
in this repository are not quotable.

> **This paragraph was itself a defect, and it is left corrected in place rather
> than rewritten.** Until 2026-09-03 it read "moved adversely all at once the
> break-even precision is 1.8382", with **no stress factor named** — on the one
> page in this repository whose subject is numbers that look fine and are wrong.
> The two stresses differ by a factor of about twenty in the break-even and
> **disagree about whether the product is viable**, so the factor is part of the
> claim and not context for it. README's own cost section had carried the full
> x1.5/x2/x2.06/x2.5/x10 sweep correctly the whole time; the summary written on
> top of it dropped the conditioning. Summarising is where conditioning gets
> lost, which is the general lesson and the reason this correction is visible.

## What is still wrong

Recorded here rather than left for a reviewer to find.

- **The primary p@k is not measured on a clean held-out split.** The
  34 cycles that produced the headline are the same
  cycles used to choose the prune strategy and the Jaccard floor. Only the
  re-ranker figures use a held-out split, and there are only
  18 of them.
- **18 held-out cycles will not resolve anything below
  about +0.05.** Most experiments in this repository return an interval that
  includes zero, and that is a property of the sample size, not of the changes.
- **The score participates in candidate generation**, so any weight change
  invalidates the candidate set. Every scorer experiment on a cached pool
  measures a fixed-candidate-set counterfactual.
- **1,917 metric-shaped literals remain unmarked in prose**,
  held against a dated ledger where every increase must carry a reason. This is
  a ratchet, not a property, and it is documented as such.
- **A historical marker is honoured on sight.** Nothing verifies that the
  sentence it exempts is actually narrating the past. That hole is named in
  `negative-results/template-literal-leak.md` rather than discovered later.
- **The negative-results append-only check covers deletion, not truncation.** A
  file could be gutted in place or have its conclusion reversed by edit and the
  test would pass.
- **FAN-IN regressed slightly under pruning** and this was not caught before
  shipping, because the sweep diagnostic ignores the real dedup and
  overlap-suppression pipeline. Flagged, not fixed.
- **The citation verifier does not check attribution.** It checks that a cited
  id exists, not that it supports the sentence. A claim with the wrong amount,
  direction or date, citing a real transaction, **passes** —
  `tests/test_citation_adversarial.py` demonstrates it on seven narratives with
  positive controls proving the two implemented checks still fire. Predicted in
  `prereg/citation_recall.md` before it was measured. Closing it needs
  claim-tuple verification and that is not built.
- **The drafted path has attempted 0 drafts**, so
  the LLM rejection rate — the only metric here that would measure the AI
  component's judgment directly — is **undefined over an empty denominator,
  not 0.0**. Every narrative number in this repository, citation recall
  included, is a property of the deterministic template.
- **`member_recall` in the citation measurement is 1.0 by construction** and
  carries a zero-width interval: the template emits every member account, so
  that component cannot vary and therefore cannot measure. It is reported with
  the tautology named rather than folded silently into the headline.
